item.title: India Panel Proposes Rules to Bring Overseas Firms Home
item.description: A panel of Indian lawmakers has proposed allowing companies registered overseas to transfer their registration to an International Financial Services Centre in India.

item.description: Public markets demand a path to profitability before they buy in

item.title: Eli Lilly Ripe for Stock Split After Obesity Drug-Fueled Rally
item.description: Wall Street’s appetite for weight-loss drug stocks over the past four years has powered Eli Lilly & Co. to consistently trade above $1,000 per share. Now, some see the pharma giant’s stock as primed for a split.

item.title: Nvidia, Dell Back AI Cloud Startup Volta at $2.4 Billion Value
item.description: Volta Infra Holdings Ltd., a new artificial intelligence cloud company, has raised $300 million in venture funding and secured an additional $5 billion worth of financing to help a wider mix of technology companies gain access to costly AI chips. The funding, set to be announced Tuesday, values Volta at $2.4 billion, and was co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Altimeter Capital. Nvidia Corp. and Michael Dell also participated. item.title: Oil Prices Can’t Fall Fast Enough for Asia to Keep Its Lights On
item.description: The Iran conflict has hit countries least equipped to absorb a global shock.

item.title: Transpacific trade and Matson shipping line
item.description: Matson shipping line expects solid demand to continue in the second half

item.title: Bending Spoons to Buy Software Firm Airtable For $2.3 Billion
item.description: App developer Bending Spoons SpA has agreed to buy software firm Airtable for an equity value of $2.25 billion, a sharp decline from the startup’s 2021 peak valuation.

item.title: India’s New Closing Auction Sparks Second Nifty Jump on Expiry
item.description: India’s first weekly derivatives expiry under the new closing auction system did little to ease concerns about the new mechanism after the benchmark NSE Nifty 50 Index again moved sharply during the auction, after surprising traders on Monday.

item.title: Bridgepoint Explores €1 Billion Private Credit Secondaries Deal
item.description: Bridgepoint Group is exploring a deal to sell more than €1 billion ($1.15 billion) of private credit stakes in a secondaries transaction, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Credit Braces for Fallen Angels as $100 Billion Trades Like Junk
item.description: Oracle Corp. and Stellantis NV are among a group of high-grade companies with debt that has recently traded close to junk levels, putting the bond market on watch for a new era of fallen angels.

item.title: Emerging Markets Stay Under Pressure as Iran Impasse Lifts Oil
item.description: Emerging-market stocks and currencies stayed under pressure as the lack of progress on US-Iran talks lifted oil prices back above $86 a barrel.

item.title: Apple Finally Gets into the Chatbot Race with Siri AI
item.description: Siri’s pre-installed status could also make it one of the world’s most widely used AI assistants almost overnight.

item.title: Apollo’s Dealmaking Spree Drives Fee-Related Revenue to a Record
item.description: Apollo Global Management reported record revenue from fees as it vies to be one of Wall Street’s largest lenders.

item.title: Brunswick Targets Record Revenue, Doubled Earnings by 2030
item.description: Brunswick Corp. expects revenue to climb to as much as $8 billion by 2030 and earnings to more than double, betting that market share gains and cost cuts will drive the bulk of growth.

item.title: A Fresh Record Looms for the Unsinkable S&P 500
item.description: Market’s gains have broadened as the AI trade falters

item.title: Crop Trader ADM Raises 2026 Outlook as Biofuels Drive Growth
item.description: Archer-Daniels-Midland Co. raised its 2026 profit outlook for a second time, as the crop trader increasingly looks to biofuels as a major driver of growth.

item.title: South Africa to List Credit-Guarantee Vehicle, Treasury Says
item.description: South Africa plans to list its first credit-guarantee vehicle that’s being established to support investment in infrastructure by private companies.

item.title: BlackRock’s Li Says AI Overweight Intact Despite Higher Risks
item.description: BlackRock Inc. remains overweight the artificial intelligence theme despite rising risks from tougher competition and higher interest rates, according to Wei Li, the firm’s global chief investment strategist.

item.title: Spotify Falls After User and Income Forecasts Miss Estimates
item.description: Spotify Technology SA shares fell in premarket trading after the world’s largest music streaming service gave disappointing forecasts for active users and operating income in the third quarter.

item.title: Ex-Nubank Executives Launch AI Wealth Adviser in Brazil
item.description: An artificial-intelligence startup founded by two former Nubank executives is launching a financial-advisory service in Brazil, encouraged by consumers’ rapid adoption of innovations such as the Pix instant-payment system and digital banking.

item.title: Italy’s Nextalia Raises €1.1 Billion for New Private Equity Fund
item.description: Italy’s Nextalia Investment Management raised over €1.1 billion ($1.3 billion) for its second private equity strategy fund, targeting opportunities in its home market.

item.title: AI Power Demands Spur Builders to Seek Billions in Bank Pledges
item.description: Power utilities across the US are already strained from AI data centers. But they’re increasingly facing an even bigger threat: that developers will be forced to walk away from projects, leaving households on the hook for massive infrastructure bills.

item.title: MediaTek-Backed African Fintech PalmPay Eyes Hong Kong IPO
item.description: Africa-focused fintech PalmPay Ltd., valued at more than $1 billion in an ongoing funding round, is preparing for a potential Hong Kong initial public offering, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: CXMT Narrows Gap With SK Hynix and Samsung in Smartphone Memory
item.description: China’s state-backed CXMT Corp. is poised to produce smartphone memory chips that are on par with the industry’s most advanced designs, highlighting the speed at which Beijing is gaining ground in a field critical for AI deployment.

item.title: Most of G-7 Is Spending More on Interest Than Defense, Scope Says
item.description: Every Group of Seven country apart from Germany and Canada now faces interest costs that exceed defense expenditure, Scope Ratings said.

item.title: Bank of Korea Minutes Back More Hikes on Inflation, Growth
item.description: The Bank of Korea saw a need for further interest-rate hikes after last month’s increase, as stronger growth threatened to keep inflation elevated and financial stability risks continued to build, minutes from July’s meeting showed.

item.title: Risk Demand Grows for Europe as AI Woes Hit US, Citi’s Chew Says
item.description: Europe’s stock market is the only major region to have experienced a meaningful improvement in risk appetite in recent weeks, supported by fresh capital inflows and better-than-expected earnings, according to strategists at Citigroup Inc.

item.title: KKR-Backed Infinx Services Said to Weigh $300 Million India IPO
item.description: Infinx Services Pvt., a healthcare revenue cycle management company, is considering an initial public offering of as much as $300 million in India, according to people familiar with the matter, joining a growing pipeline of healthcare services firms seeking to tap the country’s buoyant equity markets.

item.title: Bond Funds Turn to Europe as Global Risks Become Harder to Price
item.description: European bonds are emerging as a safer choice for fund managers as they try to navigate an increasingly fraught global backdrop.

item.title: Apple’s India Sales Top $10 Billion on Widening Retail Push
item.description: Apple Inc. exceeded $10 billion in annual sales in India for the first time last fiscal year, underscoring surging demand for its pricey devices in a market where it’s steadily ramping up its retail network.
